A. System Architecture 1. The new PAS design shall be fully redundant with dedicated network at all levels, using an audio/data star cabling structure, with hot redundancy for both the monitoring network and the digital announcement monitoring. The new PAS shall have no single point of failure. 2. The PAS shall have an active-active configuration where each PAS announcement room must be able to operate all facilities in the event that connection to the main PAS announcement room is lost. 3. The PAS shall use an industry standard software platform and configuration shall be user friendly. Trained personal shall be able to configure the system. 4. All functions such as audio processing, audio delay circuits, audio matrixes, amplifier monitoring, automatic failover switching, loudspeakers and microphone line monitoring, audio volume controls, parametric and graphic equalizers shall be part of each amplifier unit and shall be located in the PAS technical room(s). Refer to relevant PAS drawings for further details. 5. The proposed equipment shall be of rack mounted and modular assembly type in order to allow easy servicing and replacing. 6. It shall be possible to plug and unplug any PAS network equipment whatever its status in the system without causing any malfunction to the remaining system 7. Equipment repair shall be able to accomplished on site by module replacement, 8. All control components shall utilize "Distributed-Processing" concept (e.g., centralized or decentralized distribution). 9. The distributed processing must have the ability to upload operating parameters to any equipment, thus allowing full operating functions independent of any other system component. 10. The PAS shall have voice evacuation functionality to complement the FAS VES 11. Power Supply Requirements a. PAS head end equipment (e.g., servers, controller/matrix units, power amplifiers, etc.) to be powered by UPS (with redundancy). b. PAS equipment racks to be powered by two independent power supplies, that is, one from UPS as the primary power supply while the other one from a 24VDC/48VDC batteries as the secondary power supply (for redundancy) powered by an essential AC main power supply (EPS) as per NFPA code requirements. c. The secondary power supply for PAS shall be capable of operating the system under quiescent load (system operating in a non-alarm condition) for a minimum of 24 hours and then shall be capable of operating the system during a fire or other emergency condition for a period of 15 minutes at maximum connected load as per NFPA 72 code. d. All PAS active field devices (e.g., DSP controlled active line array loudspeakers, PAS call stations, BGM sources, etc.) to be powered by an UPS. 12. Comply with Section 270000.

clause: B. System Design 1. Provide a comprehensive electroacoustic study for areas covered by the PAS. 2. Coordinate the electroacoustic study with Architectural & Interior Design to ensure that the acceptable acoustic performances (ex. NRC, absorption coefficient figures, speech intelligibility, reverberation time, SPL) are achieved as per NFPA and project requirements. a. Obtain the NRC of the selected material finishes and study the acoustic performance properties. If the NRC is too low to meet the required STI, coordinate with the Architect to adjust the selection of materials and improve the NRC. b. The prediction method of the Acoustic design shall be by Ray Trace Method and be based on the following criteria: 1. Electroacoustic study by ray trace method (statistical method is not acceptable), 2. Average SPL: 80 to 85 dB with respective power amplifiers set at 60% of maximum volume, 3. Intelligibility index STI: must meet NFPA 72 criteria having STI value of at least 0.50 or greater in public areas measured without occupancy. 4. Sound diffusion level: 15 to 20 dB (A) above ambient noise level 5. Total Harmonic Distortion: a. Electronic: <= 0.2% at 1kHz at rated maximum output level. b. Acoustic: 0.3% to 0.5% at 1kHz at maximum rated output level 6. Frequency response: The measured frequency response of the system shall include a usable minimum range from f1 = 125Hz to f2 = 10kHz over 90% of the area. Below 2f1, a roll off of 12dB/octave and above f2/2, a roll-off of 6dB/octave is acceptable.

7. Uniformity of coverage: For each PAS zone, 90% of the audience area measurement points must fulfil the following criteria valid for the total sound: a. 500Hz, 1kHz and 2kHz and 4kHz octave bands shall be within ± 3dB b. 250Hz and 8kHz octave band shall be within ± 5dB 8. Conform to the latest NFPA speech intelligibility requirements. c. The use of traditional column loudspeakers in public areas may result in echo. The Contractor shall investigate delay possibilities to eliminate or reduce such echo. d. Two background noise levels shall be studied, one representing the industry standard background noise for an Airport and the second will take into consideration the additional noise generated by the smoke extraction fans during an emergency.

This fire detection and alarm system shall monitor the entire Substation areas for fires and shall display and report occurrences visually and audibly both locally at the applicable areas and centrally at Control Room.

The fire alarm system shall be completely digitally addressable interactive system, which shall distinguish between spurious fire alarms and true fire alarms in order to enhance the sensitivity of the system.
The Analogue addressable fire detection and alarm system, as installed, shall include, but not be limited to the following:

The fire alarm control panel (FACP) shall be digital addressable type having minimum of 32 zones and shall be equipped with 4 high capacity digital addressable data loops, with up to 318- address capacity per loop comprising of modules and detectors. The fire alarm control panel shall be assembled in a metal enclosure located in Control room of Substation. FACP shall be UL listed/FM approved or LPCB approved.

The fire alarm control panel and fire alarm repeater panel shall be interlinked with a central mimic panel located in Substation Security room or in the Corridor near the Substation building entrance using secure network.

The fire alarm control system shall be completely site programmable. It shall be possible to modify the commissioning configuration data by using the front keypad of FACP or by using a personal computer at site depending upon the site commissioning requirements. Necessary hardware /software except personal computer shall be supplied along with the panels to retrieve the data’s from the panel at a later date by FEWA.

The fire alarm control panel shall be compatible with printers to print real time data of fire and fault conditions including time and date of events along with device number and location text. Minimum 100 event records shall be stored in the FACP. A dedicated printer with table shall be provided.

The fire alarm control panel shall be powered with 240V AC primary power (AC) supply which will be fed from the essential supply distribution board, but the complete fire alarm and detection system shall be operating on a low voltage (nominal 24 VDC) which shall be continuously monitored by the panel.
Continuous supervision of the primary power (AC) supply, placement of alarm zone modules within the control panel, presence of battery, battery voltage and all fire alarm devices in the loop.

The system fault buzzer and system fault indication shall activate upon a single break or open condition, or ground fault, which prevents the required operation of the system. The system fault signal shall also operate upon loss of primary (AC) power supply, detector faulty, siren faulty, hooter faulty, and absence of battery, low battery voltage, and removal of alarm zone modules. Provide a system alarm silence switch, which will silence the system fault buzzer, but will not switch off the system fault indicator light. After the system returns to normal operating condition, the system fault buzzer shall again sound until the silencing switch returns to normal position.

System fault and alarm signals shall be distinctly annunciated audibly and visually, at the fire alarm control panel (FACP), including display of device type, address, zone and location with date and time of event. This information shall be recorded on the hard copy printer.
There shall be no limit, other than maximum system capacity, as to the number of addressable devices, which may be in alarm simultaneously.

The system shall be activated into the alarm mode by actuation of any alarm-initiating device. The system shall remain in the alarm mode until initiating device(s) are reset and the fire alarm control panel is manually reset and restored to normal. The actuation of initiating devices automatically initiates the following functions:

a) Display individual initiating device, location, and zone address number with alphanumeric description, which shall be as per FEWA requirements and programmed by contractor on the visual annunciation.
b) Activate indicating LED’s associated with the location and type of initiating device in alarm condition on repeater panel and mimic panels.
c) Activate indicating lamp integral to the smoke detector in alarm condition.
d) Sound an audible signal and illuminate an indicating LED’s at the FACP.
e) Record individual alarm message including device type, zone, address number and location on hard copy printer.
f) Initiate HVAC shutdown sequence.
g) Initiate Transformer cooling fan shutdown upon activation of water spray system

h) The Fire alarm system fault condition shall be annunciated to SCADA/SCMS system through Common control panel, which will be located in switchgear control room. Auxiliary contacts of compatible rating with interface equipment relays shall be provided for this purpose. A minimum three (3) numbers of volt free contacts shall be provided as a spare in main alarm control panel. Following are minimum number of signals which shall be transmitted to SCADA/SCMS system:
o Fire Protection System General Fault
o Fire Protection System General Alarm
o Fire Protection System Fire Pump Run
o Fire Protection System Deluge System Operated
o Fire Protection System Water Tank Low Level
o Clean Agent Extinguishing System Gas Discharge

Fire Control Panel:

The fire alarm control panel (FACP) shall provide power, annunciation, supervision and control for the detection and alarm system. The control panel shall be modular in construction and contain all modules necessary to operate the system according to this specification and applicable drawings.

The control panel enclosure shall be suitable for Surface mounting. A locked door shall be provided to limit access to those individuals authorized to access the panel. Locate panel with base 4 feet above the finished floor unless the panel size and ceiling height dictates a lower mounting.

All modules shall be plug-in-type, dynamically supervised, and easily replaceable. Field wiring shall be connected to the panel with removable multi-conductor connectors to facilitate rapid removal and replacement of both the module and wiring for ease of servicing the panel. Provide a copy of the system circuit diagram and control panel schematic within the control cabinet.

Long-life, light-emitting diodes (LEDs) shall be included to indicate system power (green), Fault (yellow), and alarm (red). Lamp test capability shall be provided to test all visual panel indicators and associated software.

The control panel power supply shall be capable of powering up the complete fire alarm system. All system expansion modules shall interconnect through a card edge connector and shall require no inter-module wiring.

An audible device shall sound within the control panel for alarm, supervisory, or fault. This device shall have two distinct sounds and shall be silenceable by the acknowledge/silence switch. Alarms shall override any Fault condition.

Fault and alarm shall also be annunciated on a liquid crystal display, which will give device number and location plus diagnosis of fault. Momentary contact switches shall provide for Locate, Next Alarm, Next Trouble, Acknowledge/Silence and Reset.

The control panel shall be capable of supporting addressable detection devices. The panel display shall be a minimum 80 large character, liquid crystal display and which shall provide a user-definable message associated with each detection device. Contractor shall program these data file messages prior to final system acceptance.

Each addressable detection device shall report its condition to the system control unit in a manner such that failure of the connection to or internal electronics of the device will result in a fault signal which identifies the specific device involved.

Addressable detection devices shall be individually identified by the system, and any quantity of addressable detection devices that shall be in alarm at any time shall add up to the total number connected to the system.

A liquid crystal display shall be provided to display custom message. Each device on an addressable initiating circuit shall be checked continuously to include the following: response, opens, shorts, ground faults, functionality and status. These shall be available to be recorded on system printer.
A fault signal shall be initiated for each addressable device for which the automatic sensitivity measurement is too insensitive.

The system alarm lamp shall flash upon receipt of any alarm condition Acknowledgement of the alarm by operation of the silence switch shall silence the audible alarm at the control panel and cause the alarm lamp to light steadily. Receipt of subsequent alarms shall cause the audible device to resound and the alarm lamp to flash.

The system shall automatically indicate the total quantity of alarms and of faults, which have occurred prior to reset at the control unit. No alarm or fault indication shall be resettable until it has been acknowledged. It shall not be possible to reset the system until all alarms have been acknowledged.
The control panel shall be equipped with a silence before reset feature, designed to prevent accidental system reset during an alarm condition.
Provision for control relays in the fire alarm control panel shall be included for relays having dry contacts rated at 240 VAC, 5 amps inductive.

Dynamic supervision of system electronics, wiring, detection devices and software shall be provided by the control panel. Failure of system hardware or wiring shall be indicated by type and location on the digital display. Software and processor operation shall be monitored by an independent hardware watchdog, which will indicate their failure. The system shall provide failsafe operation, i.e. incoming alarms shall automatically override all other modes of operation and the panel shall automatically return to normal operating mode from any operator-initiated mode. The system fault lamp shall flash and an integral trouble buzzer shall sound upon the occurrence of any fault condition. Acknowledgement of the fault condition by operation of the silence switch shall silence the audible alarm and cause the system fault lamp to light steadily. Receipt of subsequent system fault shall cause the system fault lamp buzzer to resound and the system fault lamp to flash.

Ground fault detection shall be provided for all initiating and indicating circuits. The control panel shall report the failure of a device's transmitting component(s) and, open or shorted, on an addressable initiating circuit. The device shall be recognized and identified by location within the circuit to the specific device, and all other devices on the circuit shall continue to function properly.

The control panel shall allow changing the status of configured circuits (arming or disarming and changing status of relays). If any change in status degrades system operation as configured, a fault condition shall be reported and remain until system operation again meets configured status.

The service mode shall permit the arming and disarming of individual detection or output devices as well as manually operating output devices. Status of these devices shall be displayed upon command from the control panel. The panel shall automatically return to the normal mode in the event the panel remains unattended in the service mode for more than 30 seconds. The system shall remain 100% operational and capable of responding to an alarm condition while in the routine maintenance mode.
The control panel shall have the ability to perform multiple operations at the same time. These operations shall include, but not be limited to, timed functions and multiple configured sequences.
Smoke, Heat Detectors & Gas detector (H2)

Suitable photoelectric type and heat detectors shall be mounted at strategic locations in the entire plant areas. On receipt of impulse from the detectors in the event of a fire, audio-visual annunciations shall be exhibited in respective annunciation panels. Any cable fault shall also be annunciated as "Cable Fault". Smoke/heat detection system shall take into consideration the ceiling beam location/depths, air velocity etc. However, listed spacing as per UL/FM/LPCB shall never be exceeded for any type of detector. Minimum of two detectors shall be provided per each room.

All detectors shall be listed and approved by LPCB or Underwriters Laboratories, Factory Mutual and UAE Civil Defence Authority. Detectors shall be supplied by reputable manufacturers or vendors approved by FEWA.

Photoelectric type smoke detectors shall be selected in accordance with the environmental conditions and anticipated combustion products in the area. Generally, smoke detectors will be suitable for the majority of areas in Substation, except in Battery Rooms, Kitchen/Pantry, and Fire pump room, where analog addressable rate of rise/fixed temperature heat detectors are required as appropriate. Also battery room shall be provided with Gas detector (H2). A multi- sensor type detector shall be considered for Cable Basements and 132kV GIS Room. Smoke and heat detectors shall be with adjustable sensitivity and address coding shall be either by software programming or, by dip/rotary switches. All detectors shall be mounted on galvanized circular box.
The set point shall be selected after giving due consideration for ventilating air velocity and electrical/electronic equipment concentration in the risk area. The set point shall be adjustable.
The detectors shall be complete with mounting base that included a terminal box into which the detector can be plugged. Terminal for looping of the cables shall be provided.

The detectors shall be provided with an in-built indicating lamp/diode to indicate operation of any detector. Response indicators at a suitable place (which is visible) shall be provided for those detectors, which are to be placed in the space above false ceiling or beneath false flooring.

Conventional rate-anticipation/probe heat detectors shall be used in Main Transformer, Earthing/Station Transformers, Reactors, and Capacitor Banks (outdoor). The detection system for these areas shall have two (2) zones and interface module shall be provided to connect probe heat detector with the fire alarm system. The modules shall be installed in weather proof interface module box installed indoor. The end of line (EOL) resistor for such detectors shall be installed in the respective areas in accessible location at least 1.2 meters from finish floor level. The detectors shall be provided with heat collector plate of disc shape of size 300mm diameter x
1.5mm thick. The heat collector plate shall be galvanized and powder coated in red colour. Detector removal Tool kit shall be provided at site & kept inside a wall mounted multi-rack,
double door cabinet inside the Fire pump room.
Manual Alarm Call Points

Addressable Manual alarm call points shall be provided at strategic locations preferably along corridors and exit points in and around the Substation. Cable Basement partition walls shall be provided with manual call points near each doors on any one side. All outdoor units including the ones installed in Cable Basements shall be weather proof type. Additionally, units installed outdoor shall be fixed with suitable sun shade. The location of manual alarm call points shall comply with UAE Civil Defence Authority requirements and further subject to approval of FEWA.
A fire alarm activation signboard shall be provided near all the Manual alarm call points as per
UAE Civil Defence Authority requirements.
Short Circuit Loop Isolators

Short circuit loop isolators compatible with the main fire alarm panel shall be provided in the signaling line circuits (SLC) between each floor of Substation, between each Cable basement, and between Auxiliary buildings. The maximum number of devices between two isolators shall not be more than twenty or as per the manufacturer’s recommendation whichever is lesser. The loop isolator in Cable basements and Fire pump room shall be installed inside weather proof IP
65 back boxes. Short circuit loop isolators shall be installed at the start and end of each SLC loop.
Sounders/Strobes

Combined Sounder/Strobe units shall be provided inside and outside the Substation complex at strategic locations. All units installed inside the Substation shall be of a similar type and tone. All sounders/strobes installed outdoor and the units intended for water spray/sprinkler system protected areas shall be weather proof type. Additionally, units installed outdoor shall be fixed with suitable sun shade.

The sound level of the sounders/strobes at any point in the Substation shall be 65 dB (A) or 5 dB (A) above any other noise likely to persist for longer than 30 seconds, whichever is the greater. If necessary, additional sounder shall be installed to meet this requirement. The intensity of light of strobe shall not be less than 75 candela (cd).

clause: For Capacitor Banks (applicable for indoor only) and LCC panels inside 132kV GIS Room, more than one hazard is to be protected from one storage facility, comprising of main and reserve cylinder bank, and each hazard shall have a selector valve in the distribution piping. For other Electrical Equipment Rooms, each room is to be protected by one local storage cylinder bank. A main/reserve transfer switch (MRTS) shall be provided for Clean Agent System with main and reserve cylinder banks. The selector valve shall be used to direct the flow of gas to respective protected room from a storage cylinder unit. The selector valve shall be provided with a piston releaser which can be opened manually or automatically through gas pressure from the actuating cylinder. The selector valve shall be installed in vertical position and shall have an option for fixing a switch (interfaced to extinguishing panel) to monitor its status. The selector valve shall be either forged or cast steel, pneumatic pilot-operated type. Resetting of control system and selector valves shall be by manual operation.
reply: Comply to all the Fire Detection & Alarm System Requirements.

clause: A safety vent shall be installed on the piping between the cylinder manifold and selector valve. The safety vent shall release the pressure in the pipe when the pressure exceeds the manufacturer’s recommended set pressure to protect the system such as piping and valves. The safety vent shall be a rupture disc type. The nozzles inlet size and orifice codes shall be determined by flow calculation software based on the final system installation. Discharge nozzles shall be made of brass-chrome plated or stainless steel and permanently marked to indicate the orifice diameter opening. The marking shall be clear view at all times and shall require no maintenance or labor to visually inspect. Discharge nozzles shall have appropriate discharge pattern and shall be sized and located to effectively cover the entire protected area and discharge Clean Agent into the area within time limit as per NFPA.

Basic Network Operation: Each FACP is a stand-alone control with direct communications into network is defined as a node. Although performing different functions, each FACP serves as a "peer-to-peer" (equal) partner in controlling network communications. Network information is sequentially transmitted from one node to another. At each node, the network message is captured and either retransmitted as received, or modified before retransmission to provide the network with a status update. The ability of the message to circulate through the network defines the network status and allows the nodes to respond accordingly. If a node goes "off-line", or if the wires between nodes either short, open, or have any other form of communication problem, the nodes will isolate that section of wiring. Nodes that cannot retransmit onto the next node of the network will transmit back to the previous node to maintain communications and to notify the network of the node status. In the event of multiple wiring problems, the remaining nodes will effectively "regroup" and establish new, smaller "sub-networks" that will maintain communications among the active nodes.

Network Media: The network is to be capable of communicating via wire or fiber optic medium. The network is to also support the use of both wire and fiber in the same network (hybrid network). A wire network is to include a fail-safe means of isolating the nodes in the unlikely event of complete power loss to a node. The fail safe design is to allow the network communications signal to bypass the failed node which allows the continuation of normal communications activity if specified wiring distances are maintained.

History File: The NRT is to be capable of storing network events in a history file. Events are to be stored on hard disk and be capable of back-up storage on a floppy disk. The history buffer is to have three modes of display. The first mode is to allow the operator to view events in a chronological order. A filter is to be available for displaying chronological events by year, month, date, time, alarms only, troubles only, alarms and troubles, security breaches, supervisory alarms, and points disabled. The second is to allow the operator to view events in a number of easy-to-read graph styles, such as, bar graph, point graph, line graph, or spline graph. Graphing is to include the ability to select alarms, troubles or alarms and troubles, then the ability to display on a by year, month, or day basis. The third mode is to allow the operator to display stored (hard or floppy disk) events in a variety of useful formats. Selections are to be available for displaying events by year, month, date, time, and alarms only, troubles only, and alarms and troubles, security breaches, supervisory alarms, and points disabled. The ability to print NRT history files is also to be available.

Graphical Information: The NRT is to include the ability to display system information in a graphical (floor plan and elevations) form. A pull-down menu is to be included allowing selection of graphical views of the facility, or subset thereof. Each view, created in a CAD environment, is to include icons created for Intelligent devices. These devices are to change in color when an event occurs. The device is to annunciate in RED when in alarm, BLUE for security activation, and YELLOW for trouble or to confirm acknowledgement. By selecting a device in the graphic presentation, the operator of the NRT is to have the ability to log onto the corresponding RAM memory and backed-up by a floppy disk memory with the possibility to compose,modify or edit the graphic schematics, text, symbols and zone allocations on-site without jeopardizing the fire alarm system operation. The unit shall be a sophisticated microprocessor based long range beam smoke detector consisting of a separate transmitter and matching receiver providing accurate and repeatable monitoring of smoke passing through the light beam.

The transmitter produces a crystal controlled, infrared beam which is monitored by the receiver to determine smoke obscuration. When the receiver measures beam intensity below a preset, selectable threshold, an alarm output is generated.

Complete beam blockage and dust accumulation that reduces signal level to 50% will initiate a trouble output. Intermittent beam blockage, such as cleaning, shall be ignored. clause: Duct Sensor: 1. It would use an Optical sensor. Housing shall include Inlet and Outlet Probes and terminations to the sensor base. Shall monitor an air flow of 100 to 1,200 m/min. in ventilation ducts. Therefore, a correct positioning of duct detectors is a must. Air turbulence caused by bends, fans or obstructions shall be fitted away from these positions. A position shall be selected where a sufficient density of smoke can reach the inlet probe. For this to be achieved, duet sensors must not be sited in a common duct as this will lead to smoke dilution. That is, air from an area of fire will mix with clean air from other areas and may not satisfactorily operate the sensor within the duct housing. When the probes are correctly aligned in the duct, the air flow along the duct promotes a pressure differential between the inlet and the exhaust probes, causing air to flow through the duct housing. If smoke is present in sufficient quantities in the duct it would be sensed by optical / heat sensor.

clause: The network inter panel wiring shall be Class A, The network media shall be copper except where fiber optic cable is specified on the drawings.

The system supplied under this specification shall utilize node to node, direct wired peer-to-peer network operations. The system shall utilize independently addressed, smoke detectors, heat detectors and input/output modules as described in this specification. The peer-to- peer network shall contain multiple nodes consisting of the command center, main controller, remote control panels, LCD/LED annunciation nodes, and workstations. Each node is an equal, active functional node of the network, which is capable of making all local decisions and generating network tasks to other nodes in the event of node failure or communications failure between nodes.

When a network is wired in a Class B configuration, a single break or short on the network wiring isolates the system into two groups of panels. Each group continues to function as a peer-to-peer network working with their combined databases. When wired using a Class A configuration, a single break or short on the network wiring causes the system to isolate the fault, and network communication continues uninterrupted, without any loss of function. Should multiple wiring faults occur, the network re-configures into many sub-networks and continues to respond to alarm events from every panel that can transmit and receive network messages.
The copper network interface shall be fire rated armored cable. The fiber optic network interface shall be fire rated armoured with single mode fiber optic transceivers.

The charger module ensures battery charging based on UI characteristics with temperature compensation according to BS-EN. The charging algorithm executed by the charger is supervised by the control module. The charger is equipped with internal active PFC module, which provides power factor close to one (λ≈1). The charger is used for charging batteries with rated voltage in the range of 120V - 216V. The maximum power of charger is 980W. If there is a need to charge a battery with higher capacity, the BST-980 charge boosters are used.

Charger module shall be boosting charge type, microprocessor-controlled module with temperaturecontrolled voltage charging to IU characteristics. It shall have charging & supervising method via battery monitoring for failure indication of battery circuit as well as battery charger. Shall have fuse protection for Mains and Battery Supply on the front face of the Charger module. Basic Network Operation: Each FACP panel has a stand-alone control with direct communications into network, and is defined as a node. Although performing different functions, each FACP serves as a "peer-to-peer" (equal) partner in controlling network communications. Network information is sequentially transmitted from one node to another. At each node, the network message is captured and either retransmitted as received, or modified before retransmission to provide the network with a status update. The ability of the message to circulate through the network defines the network status and allow the nodes to respond accordingly. If a node goes "off-line", or if the wires between nodes either short, open, or have any other form of communication problem, the nodes will isolate that section of wiring. Nodes that cannot retransmit onto the next node of the network will transmit back to the previous node to maintain communications and to notify the network of the node status. In the event of multiple wiring problems, the remaining nodes will effectively "regroup" and establish new, smaller "sub-networks" that will maintain communications among the active nodes.

Access Control Panels shall be the common term for centralized communication, distribution, and control devices utilized within the ACS. This may include various size devices, such as alarm panels, intelligent controllers, etc.
Access Control Panels (ACPs) shall be capable of operation independent from any server or central workstations, when offline shall continue in stand-alone mode.
ACPs shall include integrated power supply and closed cell battery for uninterrupted standby operation of 4-hours.
ACPs shall have batteries to retain configuration upon power failure. These shall be typically Lithium batteries with lifetime of no less than 5 years.
ACP power supply shall send a trouble signal through the ACP controller to the ACS server to notify in the event of a mains power loss to the ACP.

Access and Alarm Data database shall be uploaded/downloaded to/from the ACP automatically through the ACS server. This shall be done automatically every 12 hours. ACS shall be capable of sending a forced update, as necessary, when selected from an administrator ACS server user.
ACP firmware shall have the capability to be remotely "flashed" from the ACS server. Firmware upgrade through the replacement of on-board chips/cards shall not be accepted.
ACPs should support Wiegand output.

Signals from alarm inputs (glass break, door contact) shall appear on the ACS server and workstation within 1 second of event. When entering a door equipped with an access control reader, a card shall be presented and the unique ID code associated to the card shall be compared and analyzed from a security panel or database, which shall associate the rights to an individual. Upon access granted, the security panel shall temporarily shunt or activate power to the electrified hardware, as well as internally shunt the associated door position switch or switches for a predetermined and programmable amount of time.

Access control readers shall derive their power from the security panel or door controller therefore, the Contractor shall adhere to the manufacturer's guidelines for maximum distance from the reader to the security panel or door controller.

Access control readers shall incorporate a dual means of notification of door operation. Specifically, the access control reader shall supply an audible tone for access granted, access denied, out of service and door propped conditions. LED is usually red in normal conditions and green upon granted access.

Anti-Passback: Provide access control software capable of designating areas to require a card to enter and exit the area before it is used to enter the area again. 1) Soft and Hard Area APB: Tracks each badge that enters a specific area and defines which areas the badge may access next. 2) Door-Based APB: Tracks each badge that enters and does not allow the same badge to enter twice in a row until after the APB time limit is reached. 3) Token-Based, Timed APB: Tracks each door a badge has accessed. After the badge has accessed one door, it must access a second door or wait until the APB time limit is reached before it may access the first door again. 4) Timed Area APB: Time based hard area APB. When the time limit expires, the hard area APB becomes a soft area APB.

Technical Features: a. Connectivity: 10/100 Ethernet. Optional alternate 10/100 Ethernet (using USB/Ethernet converter). b. Security: 1) Host/Controller connection protected by TLS 1.3/1.1 or AES-256/128. 2) Controller/IO Expansion connection protected by AES. 3) Generate and load custom peer certificates for TLS. 4) Port based network access control using 802.1X. 5) Crypto memory chip. 6) HTTPS protection for installer web pages. 7) Secure cookies. 8) SNMPv3/v2c. 9) DIP switch toggle sets 5 minute time to disable web page access. 10) Disable default login credentials. 11) Authorized IP address filtering. 12) IP Client Proxy. 13) Bulk erase controller and periphery devices during replacement. 14) Strong password enforcement. c. Door Control: 1) Two-reader ports: Clock and Data, Wiegand, or RS-485. 2) Eight programmable inputs, four relays, diagnostic LEDs. d. Access Control: 1) 45,000, upgradable to 400,000 Cardholder capacity. 2) 50,000 Transaction buffer. 3) If/Then Macro capability. 4) Adjustable cardholder capacity. e. Card Formats: 1) 9 card formats per active reader, 8 per offline reader. 2) Entire card number reported on invalid read. 3) 6 digit (64-bit) User ID and 15 digit PIN numbers maximum. 4) PIV, CAC, TWIC card compatible. 5) 255 Access Levels per cardholder. 6) Activation/Deactivation Date or Date & Times. f. Card Reader Functions: 1) Multiple card format support by reader. 2) Paired reader support. 3) Alternate reader support. 4) Elevator support. 5) Turnstile support. 6) Biometric device support. 7) Open Supervised Device Protocol (OSDP) and OSDP SC compliant. 8) Occupancy count. 9) Support of multi-occupancy rules. 10) Anti-passback support - Area-based, reader-based, or time based; Nested area, hard, soft, or timed forgiveness. 11) Supports host-based approval rules. 12) Keypad support with programmable user commands, card input. 13) Shunt relay support. 14) Strike follower relay support. 15) Threat level and Operating Modes. 16) Host controlled OSDP reader passthrough. 17) Elevator floor override. g. Database Functions: 1) Encrypted database. 2) Configurable card database. 3) Supports up to nineteen (19) digit card numbers. 4) Supports pin codes up to fifteen (15) digits. 5) Card issue code of up to 32 bits, ADA and VIP flags; PIV (75 bits); Smart Card (200 bits). 6) Ability to track people and objects. h. Intrusion Alarm Functions: 1) Supports entry delays and exit delays. 2) Area monitoring. 3) Standard alarm masking. 4) Provides control and alarm processing from the keypad.

Supported Integrations: a. Regional I/O shares I/O status. b. Wireless locks. c. Map Power Supply Alarms and Events using PSIA. d. Reader firmware and configuration download. e. Supports 1 total RS-485 I/O protocols.

General Description: a. The peripheral interface device shall control two physical barriers and up to two readers (using AES-128). b. The peripheral interface device shall support a wide range of reader technologies and protocol/electrical signaling standards, including OSDP (RS-485), OSDP SC (RS-485), Wiegand (TTL), KCP (RS-485), magnetic stripe, F/2F and biometric. Wiegand and magnetic strip protocols must support one or two wire LED controls, and buzzer control. c. The peripheral interface device shall be able to utilize a cryptographic module that can encrypt/decrypt communication with the intelligent controller, supporting AES encryption using a minimum 128 bit key length. d. The peripheral interface device shall utilize a crypto memory chip that provides hardened protection of secrets such as OSDP secure channel keys.

Technical Specifications: a. The Sub-Panel is for use in low voltage, Class 2 circuits only. b. The installation of this device must comply with all local fire and electrical codes. c. Primary Power: 12-24 Volts DC +/- 10%, 550mA maximum (reader current not included). d. Intelligent Controller Communication: 2-wire RS-485 supporting 9600, 19200, 38400 or 115200 bps. e. Power: 1) 12 Vdc ± 10% regulated, 300 mA maximum each reader (input voltage (VIN) must be greater than 20 Vdc) or 2) 12 to 24 Vdc ± 10% (input voltage passed through), 300 mA maximum each reader. i. Data Inputs: TTL compatible, F/2F or 2-wire RS-485. j. RS-485 Mode: 9,600 to 115,200 bps, asynchronous, half-duplex, 1 start bit, 8 data bits, and 1 stop bit. Maximum cable length: 2000 ft. (609.6 m). k. LED Output: TTL levels, high>3 V, low<0.5 V, 5 mA source/sink maximum. l. Buzzer Output: Open collector, 12 Vdc open circuit maximum, 40 mA sink maximum. m. Card Reader Functions: 1) Multiple card format support by reader. 2) Paired reader support. 3) Alternate reader support. 4) Turnstile support. 5) Biometric device support. 6) Keypad support with programmable user commands, card input. 7) Shunt relay support. 8) Strike follower relay support. c. Power Supply Performance: a. Power Supply shall operate on a primary input of 120VAC or 208VAC through 230VAC. b. Power Supply shall be capable of supplying the maximum rated power level of 75, 150, or 250 watts at either output voltage setting of 12 or 24 volts on a continuous basis. c. Power Supply shall provide two fused output ports and be capable of electronic shutdown for protection against intermittent or sustained short circuit conditions. d. Power Supply shall provide a regulated output voltage with line voltage regulation of 0.1% and load regulation to be less than 3%.

Power Supply Features: a. Power Supply system capacity shall be expandable for a maximum of three power supply units and provide standard feature capability of power distribution, control and signaling, fire alarm interface or failsafe / fail-secure locking control. b. Power Supply system shall employ a dual buss structure for selection of output voltage on a per-output basis, across all distributed power modules. c. Power Supply system shall be capable of accepting input from a Fire Alarm Control Panel (FACP) to provide override on/off control to individually selected outputs from Normally Open or Normally Closed switch contacts as well as Voltage Application, Power Supply Return Application, or a fire alarm signaling reverse polarity signal. d. Visual indication of primary power input to the Power Supply shall indicate true presence of AC voltage on the input and not extinguish under brownout conditions.

Battery Charging: a. Power Supply shall employ an integrated dual rate battery charger with a voltage output consistent with battery manufacturers published charging voltages. b. Power Supply shall provide low battery voltage indication of degradation in excess of -10% of the battery nameplate voltage rating. c. Power Supply shall have provisions for adjusting the battery charge rate to optimize the battery charging based on amp-hour rating. d. Maximum battery capacity to be either 40 amphours for a 75 watt unit or 80 amphours for 150 or 250 watt units. e. Power Supply shall incorporate a microprocessor controlled intelligent battery charging circuit and utilize a constant current during recharge. f. Battery Presence will be implemented and indicated by generating a fault condition on the power supply and on-board visual indication.
UL Listing: a. Power Supply shall be field expandable and upgradable without compromising the UL Listing status.

Network Monitoring: a. Power Supply shall be capable of connection to a network either directly, or through a separate network interface module. b. The network monitoring module shall provide the ability of remote functionality such as control, status reporting, remote battery testing, fault reporting / restore, and shall interface with multiple control and monitoring modules to extend the remote functionality to multiple individual outputs for direct control, and extended monitoring and information gathering. c. Network connected Power Supply systems shall have the ability to be connected to a central dashboard such as MSM Enterprise for monitoring of multiple systems for enhanced analytics and real time notification.

Network Status Reporting: a. Networked Power Supply system shall have the ability to log a minimum of 1000 events, which shall be time and date stamped at the time of the event. b. Networked Power Supply system shall be able to automatically report via, email, SNMP1, 2, 3, or XML stream on the occurrence of an abnormal event or on a scheduled basis. c. Networked Power Supply system shall be capable of exporting data history in a common format, showing status and system parameters, to allow detailed data analysis.

Network Control: a. Power Supply system shall provide the ability to remotely power cycle selected outputs. b. Power Supply system shall have managed outputs that enable individual on/off control of selected outputs. c. Power Supply shall provide a remote temperature probe to monitor temperature levels of the ambient room or other devices for values outside of a parameter window set by user. d. Power Supply system shall have managed outputs with the ability to set upper and lower detection limits for load current and voltage on an individual basis.

Remote Battery Testing: a. Power Supply system shall provide the ability to remotely load test the connected battery set either manually, or as a scheduled event via network connection using the system as a load. b. Power Supply system shall measure available battery standby vs required battery standby and report through the network connection on a demand or scheduled basis.

Cyber Security: a. Networked Power Supply system shall have the capability of multiple user levels to restrict access to higher-risk settings and features. b. Networked Power Supply system shall be cyber-hardened and resistant to compromise from attacks such as synflood, DDoS, CSRF, XSS and CC. c. If the web server of a power management system is deployed to be accessible from the Internet, the web server shall support the installation of an SSL certificate issued by a Certificate Authority. Certificate logging shall be performed. d. The web server of a power management system shall keep a record of user account login. User account password shall be salted and hashed with minimum length and complexity requirements. e. The web server of a power management system shall have an administration level user account with full access privilege, and one or more levels of other user accounts with reduced access privilege. f. All files for the web server of a power management system shall require authentication for access.

Pre-wired Power Systems: a. Systems with access door controllers and associated power supplies shall be pre-wired so as to be consistently configured and labeled across the entire installation. b. Pre-wiring of the power supply and access door controllers shall consist of ac fault, system fault, tamper switch and battery connections. In addition the access door controllers shall be pre-wired for RS485 communication, system power, lock power, and lock control if present. c. The Integrated pre-wired access/power cabinet shall be UL, CUL and CE listed.

General Description: a. The reader shall offer a unique and modular concept: 1) Upscale and reuse the existing base rather than replace. 2) One common RFID core: the same electronics can be reused when adding additional functionality by simply changing the cover (standard, keypads, touch screen) and reconfigure. 3) Extension modules: Ability to upgrade the readers by adding a proxy, biometric or QR code module without replacing the existing unit. b. The reader shall be upgradable by software or firmware updates: 1) Extend the product life to its maximum/infinity. 2) Add more functionality and compatibility with existing and new RFID card technologies. c. The reader will identify users only by their badge. The access rights shall not be stored into the access control card reader. d. The reader shall be eco-friendly by design and shall be with "Zero Epoxy Resin". e. The reader must be designed and manufactured in Europe. f. Three reader customization options shall be available: 1) Logo customization on the front panel. 2) Customization of casing color. 3) "Skin Effect": customization of the casing material appearance. g. The reader shall comply with: 1) ETSI EN 300 330-2. 2) EN301 489-3. 3) EN 50364:2010. 4) IEC 60950-1:2005 A1:2009 + A2:2013. 5) IEC 62368-1:2014. 6) IK10 certified. 7) CE, FCC & UL certified. h. The reader shall come with a lifetime warranty.

Technical Specifications: i. The reader shall use an EAL5+ certified crypto processor to encrypt data and improve security and confidentiality. j. The reader shall have a buzzer that can be activated via an external command (0V) and set up to buzz automatically if a card with a configurable duration is detected. k. LEDs: 8) LED colors shall be customizable for the following statuses: standby / card detection / commanded by 0V external input. 9) The reader shall have 2 configurable high-intensity LEDs. The user can choose from up to 360 different colors. 10) LEDs can be turned off by default to make the reader less visible if necessary. The LEDs shall be on the side of the reader to be visible when the badge is present. In reader standby mode, the LEDs can be configured as follows (5 modes): off, on with fixed color, flashing, pulse mode displaying one color, rainbow mode (all colors displayed on a cycle). l. The reader shall have an option to turn on a sign of life signal (configurable) to regularly tell the system it is operating correctly. The sign of life and tamper message for the reader can be shared. m. The reader shall have a motion detector / accelerometer-based tamper protection system. The system shall be programmable with two possible actions in the event of tampering: delete security settings from the reader memory and/or send a tamper message to the system. n. The reader shall have a connector terminal for the ON/OFF relay showing tamper status. o. The reader shall have a 10-pin plug in/plug out screw connector terminal, with a 5 mm pitch. The plug in/plug out screw terminal shall not require any specific raiser or spacer. The connectors / terminals shall be resistant to "saline" environments. p. The reader shall have a removable terminal block for easy installation. q. The reader can be mounted on all types of substrate, including metal, without requiring a raiser, spacer or adapter. r. Environmental: 11) The reader's resistance to mechanical impacts must be rated IK10 minimum. 12) The reader may be installed outdoors or indoors and must have water and dust ingress protection equivalent to IP65 rating (excluding connectors) - waterproof electronics. 13) The reader shall have a size up to 107 x 80 x 26 mm (H x W x D). 14) The reader operating temperature range shall be down to -30°C and up to +70°C with allowable humidity between up to 0 - 95%. 15) The reader power supply range shall be from +7VDC to +28 VDC - Typical Voltage 12V. 16) Power consumption at 12 VDC shall be (maximum values): up to 130 mA for a single reader. 17) The reader shall be compatible with European and US electrical boxes.

Reader Technology: a. The reader shall operate at a frequency of 13.56 MHz and will use Bluetooth Smart Technology BLE 4.0 and NFC. b. The reader shall be capable of reading Mobile IDs using Bluetooth from an existing mobile application, available for free on the market stores Google Play and Apple Store. c. The reader shall support the following technologies: 1) ISO 14443A. 2) ISO 14443B. 3) ISO 18092. 4) Bluetooth 4.0 Low Energy. 5) NFC Host Card Emulator (HCE). d. The reader shall read the following card technologies: 1) MIFARE Classic & Classic EV1. 2) MIFARE Ultralight, Ultralight C. 3) MIFARE Plus. 4) LEGIC Advant. 5) MIFARE DESFire EV1, DESFire EV2, DESFire EV3. 6) NFC. 7) SMART MX. 8) CPS3. 9) Moneo. 10) I.Class. 11) PicoPass. e. The reader shall by default comply with MIFARE DESFire EV2 and EV3 standards ISO 14443-4, including the new security mechanisms: 1) Secure Messaging EV2: secure transaction method based on AES-128 with protection against interleaving and replay attacks. 2) Proximity Check: improved protection against relay attacks. f. Secure readers can be configured to manage and support the various types of encryption or authentication keys and algorithms that are used with each chip technology. AES 128-bit, DES/3DES, Crypto1, HMAC-SHA1 and SHA2, RSA 2048-bit algorithms. g. Key diversification algorithms compliant with recommendation: 1) NXP AN-10922. 2) NXP AN 165310. 3) Diversification AV1.

Reading Modes: a. Using the physical / plastic badge, the following shall be the reading range values for the reader - Credit-card size badge (ISO) with chip: Mifare Classic/UL: 8 cm (CSN); Mifare DESFire EV1/Plus: 6 cm (CSN) - 2.5 cm (private ID with AES security); Mifare DESFire EV2/Plus: 6 cm (CSN) - 6 cm (private ID with AES security); Mifare DESFire EV3/Plus: 6 cm (CSN) - 6 cm (private ID with AES security). b. Mobile ID (Virtual Credentials): 1) The mobile application containing the virtual access badges must be compatible with smartphones running on iOS and Android. This should be able to be downloaded and installed from the AppStore and the Playstore. 2) Using a Mobile ID (or Virtual credential), the reader will read virtual credentials through NFC (Android) or Bluetooth BLE (Android and IOS). The reading distances can be adjustable per configuration. The reader shall read the virtual card while the smartphone is locked or unlocked by the user. 3) The reader shall accept up to 6 identification modes using the smartphone: Card mode (up to 30 cm); Slide & Pass mode (up to 90 cm); Tap-Tap mode (up to 15 meters); Hands-free mode (up to 10 meters); Remote mode (up to 20 meters); Voice command mode. 4) The reader shall feature an internal capacitive detection sensor without additional modules in order to use the SLIDE mode in Bluetooth, without touching the reader. This detection can be coupled to an internal relay on the reader during a specific integration. 5) The Mobile ID solution shall allow the holder of the smartphone to be authenticated before any identification. Several security levels can be configured (high/intermediate/low). 6) The smartphone containing the Virtual access badges protects the data stored in the smartphone using encryption methods and obfuscation, using RGS-compliant public methods and algorithms (AES-256 and SHA-2). 7) The smartphone user application shall use an AES 256 encrypted database. 8) The master key of the application shall not be stored within the smartphone application; regenerated each time authentication is needed, using Keystore on IOS and the Android Keychain. 9) The security of the Bluetooth configuration badges must be able to be controlled using the offline encoding station. 10) There shall exist two deployment modes - OFFLINE (on local stations only, no internet, Windows environment) and ONLINE (external internet connection, remote manage/create/update/revoke/send virtual badge). 11) The entire platform must be stored in a high-security data center monitored 24/7, ISO 27001 and PCI-DSS certified, secured HTTPS TLS v1.2. 12) The Mobile ID solution shall be based on a non-recurring fees business model; only a per-per-use model shall apply. 13) The online platform can be controlled using third-party software via a WEB API REST type link, free and available on request with full API documentation.

Reader Compatibility: a. The reader shall have a TTL or RS485 interface. b. The TTL interface can be configured to communicate using Wiegand or Data/Clock protocol and can transmit data with data lengths of 1 to 48 bytes (Wiegand). c. With Wiegand, data can be AES-encrypted with a customizable key. d. RS485 interface: 1) The RS485 interface can transmit data from 1 to 48 bytes. 2) With the RS485 version, the reader shall be compatible with secure protocol SSCP V1 or V2. 3) With the RS485 version, the reader shall be compatible with OSDP protocol, V1 and V2. 4) With RS485, the reader can be connected to security interfaces to provide an AES-encrypted connection with a customizable key or make the reader "transparent".

Reader Programing: a. Security and operating settings can be configured using an SCB-type programming card. b. Reader operating settings can be configured either using a physical programming card or a virtual programming card. c. The configuration for reading each type of supported chip shall be independent. The reader may have a specific behavior for each chip. Users can define what is read (data), where it is read (locations) and how it is read (keys, protections) for each technology. Users can also permit or prohibit any supported technology from being read. d. Using a virtual configuration card, the programming application must be compatible with smartphones running on iOS and Android. e. The Mobile ID solution must offer a smartphone configuration application containing the master configuration badges for the readers. f. All reader and badge protection and configuration keys must be user-managed and user-customizable. The reader shall not use any proprietary key. Firmware updates shall be available to download via the reader's serial connection using a secure communication method. g. Reader configuration may be protected with a user-defined key. Once they have been configured, the only way to change the configuration is to use programming badges created with this key.

Access control and monitoring software shall meet, at minimum, the following requirements: a. Intelligent Controllers: 250 per appliance allowing geographic independence from appliance via IP communication. b. Access Control System Appliances Supported: Up to 100 using replication. c. Events Stored: Up to 150,000,000. d. Sub-Panels: Up to 15 per intelligent controller. e. Doors: Up to 32 per intelligent controller. f. PIN Length: Between 2 and 8 digits. g. Card Formats: Up to 128 per appliance. h. Time Schedules: 255 per intelligent controller. i. Holidays: 255 per intelligent controller. j. Identity and Operator Database: 45,000 and optional Up to 4,000,000. k. Client Connections: Up to 50. l. Collaborations and Integrations: 1) Database Collaborations and Integrations - Bidirectional: LDAP/Active Directory, SQL Server, Oracle RDBMS, CSV, REST API Integration. Push Only: XML for Event Push. 2) Visitor Management Integrations. 3) Video Integrations. 4) Custom Integrations: Destination Dispatch; Custom Integrations using RestAPI (as needed for project requirements).

Software Interface: a. Web-Based Access Support: Provide access control software with browser-based access to system applications including support for industry standard desktop and mobile web browsers. b. Tabbed User Interface: System supports the following functionality in a tabbed view: 1) Monitor events, alarms, and hardware status in real time. 2) Verify identities in real time. 3) Search historical events and alarms. c. Events and Alarms: Provide a system that allows administrators the ability to create, configure, and prioritize events and alarms and communicate information about the generation of the event or alarm to the operator with guidance for responding to the event or alarm. Events will support two levels: system level events affect all objects in the system; field level events affect only the object they are configured on. d. Access Groups: Provide a system that allows administrators the ability to create groups of card readers and schedules such that card readers can allow or restrict access to areas based on schedules. e. Identity Records: Provide a system with integrated identity management, allowing imports of data from supported databases. Each identity supports access control based on groups and roles as well as individual overrides. Include functionality to customize identity and token forms in base software. Provide identity records capable of management and synchronization between multiple sites. f. Roles: Support a role-based permission method allowing one or more roles to be assigned to identities to determine physical and logical access. g. Anti-Passback: Provide access control software capable of designating areas to require a card to enter and exit the area before it is used to enter the area again. 1) Soft and Hard Area APB. 2) Door-Based APB. 3) Token-Based, Timed APB. 4) Timed Area APB. h. Badging: Provide a tool to support the creation of custom badge layouts including: 1) Static Information: Badge size, background color, text strings, and graphics common to every badge. 2) Dynamic Information: Text fields and images from the identities database unique to each badge. i. Enrollment: Provide integrated identity management and enrollment functionality as part of the core system functionality. j. Macros: Provide a system capable of linking one or more events to macros such that a single event may execute up to 30 macros. System must support a minimum of 255 macros per intelligent field controller. k. Device Template Configuration: Provide an access control system that supports templates to automatically populate standard parameter fields in groups for new or existing doors, wires, readers, and input/output devices. l. Encryption: Provide access control system that supports the following encryption methods: 1) TLS 1.2: Require TLS encryption between the access control system and controller. 2) Custom Certificates: Require self-signed or certificate authority certificate to harden access control systems. Certificates will authenticate panels to the access control system. m. Custom Device Mappings: Administrators may assign a unique group of alarm attributes to specific device-alarm combinations to override global settings of generic attributes. n. Dashboard: Allow creation of a dashboard for real-time status and actions of hardware components on a single screen that can also filter by name, status, appliance, or group. 1) Hardware Status: Panels, Sub-Panels, Inputs, Outputs, Doors, Appliances. 2) Monitor: Panels, Sub-Panels, Inputs, Outputs, Power Supplies, Access Control Doors. 3) Manipulate Access Control Doors: Door actions, Door mode, Door Forced, Door Held, Installed. o. Map Interface: Provide interface for creating customizable layouts including floorplans, reader locations, and buttons that can trigger actions. 1) Actions. 2) Occupancy/Mustering. 3) Programmable Buttons. p. Verification Interface: Provide web-browser-enabled connection to access control software allowing a user to review information about card holders entering or exiting up to four (4) doors in real time. Information to include badge photo, transaction time, and date via any device with a compatible browser. q. Virtual Verification Station: Provide web-browser-enabled connection to the access control software to allow a user to visually confirm the identity and authorization of a person attempting entry to a controller area via a mobile device such as a tablet or smartphone. r. Access Control Software Reporting: Generate, filter, edit, and customize system reports including the automated generation and distribution of customized reports in PDF and CSV formats.

Software Administration: a. Backup: Provide access control software capable of backing up via USB drive, local appliance, windows network share, or secure copy protocol. b. Database Replication: Replicate database from 1 to 100 appliances for distributed identity control. c. Updates: Provide access control software capable of automatically updating the following: d. Operating System: Version, service packs, and security vulnerabilities. 1) Field Devices: Firmware versions. 2) Upgrade Functionality: Provide access control software capable of automatically upgrading software licensing.

Request to Exit Push Buttons shall be provided at the locations shown on the security drawings. Pushbuttons shall meet, at minimum, the following requirements: a. Spring loaded momentary action. b. "PUSH TO EXIT" in bold lettering on stainless steel faceplate. c. Mushroom button style (recessed buttons shall not be permitted).

Provide three thousand (3000) access cards to the Employer. Cards shall meet, at minimum, the following requirements: a. Credit card sized ISO standard. b. Constructed of a durable P.V.C. material, white in color. c. Capable of vertical slot punching. d. Capable of accepting direct printing based video image application to allow the access card to be used as an employee ID card. e. Encoded with a unique identification code. f. Card number printed on the card. g. Compatible with the ACMS and the Guest Room Access Control System. h. Coordinate card requirements with the Employer.
A set of door contacts shall be provided for doors that are monitored in the locations as indicated in the layout drawings.
The door alarms shall be integrated with the Security Management Software.
Door alarms shall be operated by proximity switches, discreetly mounted and designed to minimize "by-passing". Where fitted to fire doors, the integrity of the fire door rating shall be maintained.
Door alarms shall be displayed on a monitor located in the Security control room.

The system shall provide the following monitoring functions: a. Interfaced to the Video Surveillance System to the extent that the image from adjacent cameras is displayed on receipt of a door alarm alert. b. Alarm read out, identifying time & alarm point. c. Manual override of any selected door. d. Automatic override of any selected door as a function of time. e. Audio & visual alarm with audio alarm switching (mute). f. Supervised circuits to identify faulty (tampered) circuits.

The Bollard should be physically crash tested under ASTM/DOS/PAS 68/IWA 14:2013 std wherein it should withstand the front impact of minimum 6.8 Ton (or more) vehicle traveling at the speed of 48 kmph. A physical crash test report is to accompany the bid.
Height of the bollard should be minimum 900mm.
For better aesthetics the diameter of the bollard should be 200mm or less.
The foundation of the shallow mount Static Bollard should be 125 mm or lesser.
The Bollard should have a vehicle penetration of less than 1 Mtr or P1 Penetration in the physical crash test certificate.

1. The automatic feedback controller shall be a single channel digital signal processor with twelve 1/10- or 1/5- octave filters (selectable). It shall automatically sense feedback and determine its pitch, then assign a digital notch filter to the resonating frequency to automatically eliminate the feedback.

The MIC/LINE Channels
In the mixer section, a total of 8 channel strips are available: 4 MIC / LINE channels, 2 MIC / Stereo USB channels ('Super Channels') and 2 stereo LINE channels.

The MIC / LINE channels offer extremely low-noise and low-hum electronically balanced XLR microphone inputs with an extremely low distortion factor (typ. 0.002%) for the connection of lowimpedance microphones. For condenser microphones, phantom power (+48 volts) is centrally switchable. The LINE inputs are also electronically balanced and implemented as TRS sockets. In addition to a Gain control, a highly efficient 3-band equalizer, FX send, AUX send and a Monitor send as well as either Panorama or Balance controls are available. The four MIC / LINE channels provide a switchable 80Hz Lo-Cut filter to cut-off unwanted rumble, whilst the Super Channels 5-6 and 7-8 are supplied by the USB stereo inserts 1-2 and 3-4.

The STEREO-LINE channels (9-10 and 11-12) offer electronically balanced TRS inputs for the connection of electronic instruments such as keyboards, drum-computers, guitars and basses with active electronics, as well as all other high-level stereo signal sources such as additional mixers, effects devices etc. CD or MP3 players can be connected to the additional cinch (RCA) inputs CD 1-2 and CD 3-4, which are switched in parallel. The tone controls and sends are identical to those of the MIC / LINE channels.

All input channels, provide a Signal / Peak LED to assist level control. The SIG LED illuminates at around -30 dB and the PK LED at 6dB beneath the distortion threshold. A MUTE button and a PFL button (in channels 5-12 in stereo) are further features found in all input channels.
The DIGITAL AUDIO Interface

The DIGITAL AUDIO INTERFACE features two stereo channels, present as USB 1-2 and USB 3-4 in Super Channels 5-6 and 7-8 respectively. This professional interface is implemented with 24-bit resolution and sampling rates up to 96 kHz, satisfying studio requirements. The USB sends are supplied with the Master L and R, AUX and MON signals. The DIGITAL AUDIO INTERFACE can be used for input and output simultaneously. Via the USB 2.0 port of your PC / Mac, four channels can be transmitted simultaneously in each direction. When a USB 1.1 interface is used, two channels can be transmitted simultaneously in each direction. The CMS is designed for the level of standard PCs / Macs; the gain level can easily be adjusted from the connected computer. Included in the delivery is an instruction sheet and a licenses code for the Cubase LE software.
PC MIDI Interface
The CMS includes a fully-featured PC MIDI interface. The MIDI input also supports the remote switching of both internal effects units using a master keyboard or MIDI footswitch.

Master Section features the Master A L+R sends (on separate faders), an additional Master B send (switchable pre/post master A and mono/stereo), the stereo effects returns, and the master sends of the AUXiliary and MONitor busses. If the AUX buss is not used to supply FX 2, it can be switched pre or post fader to use as an additional monitor or FX send.

The 9-band stereo equalizer in themaster section allows you to adjust the frequency response to the acoustics of the room. The REC SEND and USB OUT controls determine the level of the master L+R signal at the Rec Send sockets and in the output channels of the digital USB interface. PHONES allows you to adjust the volume of the headphones output.

Two ten-LED meters provide an overview of the power amplifier level. When the PFL switch is activated, the left-hand LED chain shows the internal level of the master buss in dBu. The STANDBY switch mutes all outputs with the press of a single button. For the playback of e.g. background music, the DEVICE SETUP menu allows you to route stereo channel 11-12 for standby operation directly to the power amplifiers.

BCD : In addition to other modes of clock synchronization, the MTC shall also transmit a Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) Digital signal containing the Hour, Minute, and Second, and shall transmit this signal once each second. This signal shall utilize Twisted Shielded # 18 pair, Belden 8760 or equivalent, and shall be able to transmit the data up 25,000 feet. Amplifiers shall be utilized for extension of the system beyond this limitation, Twisted Telephone pairs may be used up to 5,000 feet. Clocks designed for operation utilizing this signal shall revert to the correct time within one second of the restoration of the ACP Power. This Signal may also be used, via an RS-232 Converter module, for the purpose of synchronizing Inlet personal computers.

Impulse : The MTC shall, via an optional, have the capability to synchronize 24 VDC or 48VDC 2 or 3 wire Impulse Clocks. Once each hour, during the 59th minute, the MTC shall transmit up to (70) rapid impulses to the clock purchase of synchronizing each clocks minute hand. Only those clocks, which are in disagreement with the MTC, shall be affected. Additionally, the Impulse module shall include an accumulator for the purchase of measuring missed impulses during power failure. As soon as power is resumed. the impulse module shall release these missed impulses to the system, bringing the system back in agreement with the MTC. The rate of rapid impulses may be adjusted to a slower rate if Tower Clock are to be controlled. The Impulse module shall, if so designated, be able, via dipswitch selection, to control compatible clocks manufactured by others.

Synchronous-Wired : Once each hour, during the 58th minute, the MTC shall transmit a (8) second signal to the clock circuits for the purpose of synchronizing each clocks minute and second hands. Only those clocks, which are in disagreement with the master, shall be affected. At 5:58 AM & PM,the MTC shall transmit at 14 second signal to the clock circuits, which shall synchronize the Hour, Minute and Second hands, Any clock, regardless of the length of power failure, shall be brought in synchronization with the MTC.

Power Line Carrier: once each hour, during the 58th minute, the MTC shall transmit a (8) second signal to the model 6850/2850(s) Signal Generators which shall superimpose a high frequency signal on the 60 HZ Distribution for the purpose of sychronizing each clocks minutes and second hands. Only those clock, which are in disagreement with the MTC.shall be affected. Wiring from each clock back to the MTC shall not be required .Each clock shall be eqipped with a receiver tuned to the frequency of the Signal Generators and wired to the nearest un-switched source pf 120 VAC. at 5;58 AM & PM, the MTC shall transmit a 14 second signal in a similar process, which shall synchronize the Hour, Minute and Second hands. Any clock, regardless of the length of the power failure, shall be brought in synchronization with the MTC. B. Description: the fire alarm system is to be composed of a main fire alarm control panel FACP.
C. System Supervision: to automatically detect and report to FACP open circuits, shorts, and grounds of wiring for initiating device, signalling line, and notification-appliance circuits.

D. Type: fire alarm system is to be class A, 2-wire/4 –wire audibly and usually supervised analogue addressable, zoned, non-coded system. Manual stating, automatic fire detectors, sensors circuits and interface devices (control modules, monitor modules and fault isolators) are to be grouped in loops.

E. Priority of Signals: automatic alarm response functions resulting from an alarm signal from one zone or device are not to be altered by subsequent alarm, supervisory, or trouble signals. An alarm signal is the highest priority. Supervisory and trouble signals have second- and third-level priority. Higher-priority signals take precedence over signals of lower priority, even when the lower-priority condition occurs first. Annunciate and display all alarm, supervisory, and trouble signals regardless of priority or order received.
F. Interference: a signal on one zone is not to prevent the receipt of signals from other zones.
G. System Reset: all zones are to be manually resettable from the FACP and after initiating devices are restored to normal.

H. System Alarm Capability during Circuit Fault Conditions: system wiring and circuit arrangement are to prevent alarm capability reduction when a single ground or open circuit occurs in an initiating device circuit, signal line circuit, or notification-appliance circuit.

I. Loss of primary power at the FACPs is to initiates a trouble signal at the associate SFAC and the FACP. The FACPs is to indicate when the fire alarm system is operating on the secondary power supply.
J. Basic Alarm Performance Requirements: operation of automatic alarm of a smoke or heat detector device is to initiate the following:
1. Identification at the FACP of the device originating the alarm.
2. Audible and visible indication of an "alarm verification" signal at the FACP.
3. Recording of the event in the system memory of the FACP.
4. Recording of the event by the system printer.
5. If no cancellation is received within a pre-set time, or if a second notification is received, the following is to be initiated:
a. Release of fire and smoke doors held open by magnetic door holders in the zone of fire. (Refer to Arch. Division).
b Send signal to the BACS to shutdown fans and other air-handling equipment and to close smoke dampers in air ducts of system serving fire zone .
c. Shutdown the public address system and separate local sound systems located at the same zone.
d. Automatic dialing to the fire brigade.
e. Send an evacuation message to the fire zone.
f. Send an alert message to all adjacent zones to fire zone.
g. Release of the parking gate
h. A sequence of evacuation messages specified in the cause and effect matrix unless interruption from FACPs, will be initiated until complete evacuation of the building.
i. The interval time between two evacuation messages will be programmed such that there is sufficient time to evacuate a complete zone of fire.
j. Recording of the event in the system memory.
K. Basic Alarm Performance Requirements: operation of a manual station or operation of a sprinkler flow device is to initiate the following:
2. Audible and visible indication of an “Alarm Verification” signal at FACP.
3. Release of fire and smoke doors held open by magnetic door holders in the zone of fire.
4. Send signal to the BACS to shutdown fans and other air-handling equipment and to close smoke dampers in air ducts of system serving fire zone
5. Recording of the event in the system memory.
6. Recording of the event by the system printer.
L. Send signal to the PLC System to shutdown fans and other air-handling equipment serving fire zone when duct smoke detector is initiated.
M. Alarm Silencing, System Reset and Indication: controlled by switches in the FACP.
1. Silencing-switch operation is to halt alarm operation of notification appliances and to activate an "alarm silence" light. Display of identity of the alarm zone or device is to retained.
2. Subsequent alarm signals from other devices or zones are to reactivate notification appliances until silencing switch is operated again.
N. Water-flow alarm switch operation is to initiate the following: 1. Notification-appliance operation. 2. Flashing of the device location-indicating light for the device that has operated.

O. Fire-pump power failure, including a dead-phase or phase-reversal condition, reported from BAC is to initiate the following: 1. A supervisory, audible, and visible "fire-pump power failure" signal indication at the FACP and the annunciator. 2. Recording of the event by the system printer.
